title: Generalized Weakness

rationale.Physical Exam: General Appearance: Assess for edema, respiratory distress from fluid overload.
rationale.Physical Exam: Chest / Lungs: Recent strep infection — assess for pneumonia signs.
rationale.Physical Exam: Extremities: 2+ pitting edema around ankles — classic nephritic finding.
rationale.Urinalysis with microscopy: Dysmorphic RBCs, RBC casts (pathognomonic), proteinuria (nephritic range <3.5g/day). Cola-colored urine from hematuria.
rationale.BMP / CMP: Elevated BUN/Cr — acute kidney injury. Hyperkalemia possible.
rationale.C3, C4 complement: Low C3 (returns to normal in 6-8 weeks). C4 normal — distinguishes PSGN from other GN.
rationale.ASO titer / Anti-DNase B: ASO elevated after strep pharyngitis. Anti-DNase B after skin infection.
rationale.Renal ultrasound: Normal or slightly enlarged kidneys. Rule out obstruction.
rationale.Furosemide (Lasix): Loop diuretic for edema and hypertension management.
rationale.Antibiotics (Penicillin) if active strep: Treat active streptococcal infection. Does not alter course of GN but prevents spread.
rationale.Immunosuppression (steroids / cyclophosp: PSGN is self-limited, immune complex-mediated. Immunosuppression is NOT indicated. Supportive care only — spontaneous recovery in 95%+ of children.

hpi: {{patient_name}} is a child who presents with generalized weakness, oliguria, cola-colored (dark brown) urine, periorbital and ankle edema (2+ pitting), and hypertension 1-4 weeks after a streptococcal pharyngitis or skin infection (impetigo). This is acute poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis — an immune complex-mediated (type III hypersensitivity) disease. Antigen-antibody complexes deposit in the glomerular basement membrane → complement activation → glomerular inflammation. Labs: UA shows hematuria (dysmorphic RBCs, RBC casts — pathognomonic), proteinuria (<3.5g/day — nephritic, not nephrotic range). Low C3 complement (returns to normal in 6-8 weeks). Elevated ASO titer (pharyngitis) or anti-DNase B (skin infection). BMP shows elevated BUN/Cr (acute kidney injury). Diagnosis is clinical. Renal biopsy only if rapidly progressive GN or atypical course. Treatment: supportive — salt/fluid restriction, diuretics (furosemide) for hypertension and edema, antihypertensives if needed. Prognosis excellent in children (>95% complete recovery). Antibiotics if active strep infection. No immunosuppression needed.
